outcome: Maternal cardiovascular events (heart failure, ventricular tachyarrhythmias, pregnancy-induced hypertension, HELLP/preeclampsia)
cohort: The study included 421 women with surgically repaired Tetralogy of Fallot who became pregnant, participating in the international ESC EORP Registry Of Pregnancy And Cardiac disease (ROPAC).
finding: Women with repaired Tetralogy of Fallot generally tolerate pregnancy well, with no maternal mortality and a low complication rate, although pulmonary regurgitation is significantly associated with RV dilatation, and fetal/neonatal outcomes are favorable.
mod_finding: Almost half (48%) of the women underwent a Caesarean section, with the authors suggesting that more women could likely have had a vaginal delivery.
